tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Mean absolute Surface Distance
95% Hausdorff distance
Dice Score

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

For mitral valve leaflet segmentation, surface distance metrics are the preferred choice due to the long, thin nature
of the leaflets. This can result in the Dice score being misrepresentative if the entire leaflet segmentation is shifted



 Segmentation of the Mitral Valve from 3D Transesophageal Echocardiography

slightly, while the surface distance will remain low. This better agrees with expert judgement on the correctness of
a segmentation.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

1) MASD, 95% HD, and Dice scores are computed for each case
2) Mean of each metric is computed across all cases
3) Rankings will be calculated per metric
4) Final ranking determined by averaging per-metric rankings, with a tie being awarded to the submission with the
lower MASD score.

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

Any submission with missing output on any case will be excluded from the leaderboard.Valid submissions require
output for every case.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

This ranking scheme is used to create a balanced ranking that accounts for both surface distance and Dice score
metric. Expected surface distance results fall into the 0.5-2mm range, and will contribute more to the final score
than the Dice metric will. This aligns with the surface distance metrics giving more representative information
than Dice. The inclusion of both MASD and 95%HD ensure consistency of the given model, as MASD is low if most
of the segmentation matches well, but does not capture small areas with large discrepancy, with the 95%HD
provides information on largest discrepancies that can be found within the prediction.
